subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw use when an active session transcript is too large or repeatedly crashes the gateway on reload?
rationale: The code can prove the current unbounded load boundary, but choosing between skip/quarantine, automatic compaction, destructive truncation, or opt-in-only behavior determines data preservation and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Default quarantine or successor recovery
options.body: Mark the session degraded before full replay and move future turns to a safe successor or quarantine path with doctor-visible recovery guidance.

options.title: Bootstrap amplifier only
options.body: Land only the bootstrap marker circuit breaker and leave oversized transcript recovery to manual operator cleanup or existing opt-in compaction settings.

options.title: Config-gated strict mode
options.body: Keep current default behavior and add an explicit strict recovery option, accepting that existing users can still hit the crash loop until they opt in.

recommendation.title: Default quarantine or successor recovery
recommendation.body: Mark the session degraded before full replay and move future turns to a safe successor or quarantine path with doctor-visible recovery guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session serialization, repair, and compaction-adjacent history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the recovery-policy decision.
